title: You are my witnesses (Sifre Deuteronomy 346)
hook: a daring midrash: when you are My witnesses, I am God
tomorrow: a man drills a hole under his own seat. whose problem is it?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Torah given in the desert: free as fire and water, for anyone who makes themselves open. Free as the wilderness. Today the week comes back, with one daring line to hold it together.
screen: `FREE AS THE WILDERNESS.` → `THE WEEK COMES BACK.`

segments.voice: A screenshot in a group chat, a friend who says I was there, I saw it. A witness turns a rumor into something that happened. Witnesses don't make a thing true; they make it known. Isaiah has God say to Israel: "ye are My witnesses, saith the LORD, and I am God." Read quickly, it's a statement. The Sifre reads it slowly, as an if, and the answer to yesterday's question is almost too bold to say out loud.
screen: `I WAS THERE. I SAW IT.` → `YE ARE MY WITNESSES.` → `READ IT AS AN IF.`

segments.voice: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai says: when you are My witnesses, I am God. And when you are not My witnesses, I am, as it were, not God. That as it were, kivyakhol, is the rabbis' own safety rail, the word they reach for when a teaching nearly tips over. Nobody here says God stops being. The daring part is about the name: how God is known in the world rides on whether people live like witnesses. It's a sentence a parent could say at dinner when a kid asks where God is: people learn who God is partly by watching us. And look back at this week. It turns out to be a list of how. As He is, be: gracious and merciful. Walk in His ways: clothe, visit, comfort, bury. Offered to all: a yes you chose. The world held its breath: a still place for big words. Each according to strength: one voice, fitted to every listener. Free as the wilderness: open, and owned by no one. Six ways of bearing witness, and not one of them is a speech. Each one is something a person does, in a room, with other people watching.
screen: `WHEN YOU ARE MY WITNESSES.` · `KIVYAKHOL: AS IT WERE.` · `THE NAME, KNOWN THROUGH PEOPLE.` · `SIX WAYS, NO SPEECHES.` · then, large: `YOU ARE MY WITNESSES.`

segments.voice: Count on your fingers three moments this week when you saw someone act like a witness: a kindness, a visit, a fair word, a door held open. For each one, say the person's name to yourself, slowly, and see their face. If one of those moments was yours, it counts too.
screen: `THREE MOMENTS.` · `A NAME FOR EACH.` · `YOURS COUNTS TOO.`

segments.voice: You are my witnesses: the Sifre's daring reading of Isaiah. When you are My witnesses, I am God; and when you are not, as it were, not.
Keep this one: you are my witnesses. Six small ways this week, and none of them needed a microphone.
